answer: Rate-limit identity creation and tie each new identity to proof of unique personhood: one verified human may mint only a few agent identities per week, and each mint requires a fresh liveness check that cannot be replayed or farmed. Like a meadow that can only grow so many new shoots each season, the garden of identities stays small enough to inspect. A sybil farmer must then pass a costly human check for every fake, and the echo of repeated failures flags their whole batch, so the attack's cost scales with its size instead of staying flat.
